text: Debugging is a crucial skill for any programmer. When your code doesn’t work, the first step is identifying the bug. Instead of guessing, take a systematic approach: reproduce the error, then narrow down which part of the code is causing it. Many tools make this easier, such as breakpoints in an integrated development environment (IDE) or using a debugger to step through your code line by line. Another powerful technique is logging. By adding print statements or writing messages to a log file, you can track variable values and see where the logic fails. Remember, patience is key—most bugs are simple mistakes that a clear, step-by-step method will quickly reveal.
